sentences.text: Heard on I.A.No.7484 of 2024, an application for dispensing service of notice to respondent No.1.
After due consideration, the same is allowed and service of notice upon the respondent No.1 is dispensed with at the risk and cost of learned counsel for the appellant himself.
I.A.No. 7484 of 2024 is accordingly disposed off.
With the consent of the parties, matter is heard finally at motion stage.

2. This appeal has been filed by the appellants under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 09.11.2022 passed in MACC.No.08/2021 by IInd Additional M.A.C.T.,
Maihar, District- Satna seeking enhancement of compensation.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that Tribunal has determined deceased's monthly income as Rs.4,125/-, whereas in view of minimum wages fixed under Minimum Wages Act,
deceased's monthly income should have been determined as Rs.7,950/-.

It is also urged that Tribunal has awarded only Rs.44,000/- for consortium, whereas, appellants being son/daughter/parents of deceased, each is entitled to receive Rs.40,000/- as consortium and appellants are also entitled to receive Rs.15,000/- each for loss of estate and funeral expenses.
On above grounds, it is urged that compensation awarded by the Tribunal be suitably enhanced.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the appellants and perused the record of the case.

5. So far as deceased's monthly income on the date of accident is concerned, it is well established that when, in the facts & circumstances of the case, actual income of deceased is not established,
then, court would determine deceased's monthly income on the basis of minimum wages as notified under Minimum Wages Act.

6. Perusal of impugned award reveals that Tribunal has determined deceased's monthly income,
treating deceased as an unskilled labour.
On the date of accident, minimum wages of an unskilled labour, notified under Minimum Wages Act, were Rs.7,950/-.
Hence, deceased's monthly income is determined as Rs.7,950/-.

Tribunal has only awarded Rs.44,000/- for loss of consortium, whereas,
each appellants are entitled to receive compensation @ Rs.40,000/- for loss of consortium.

7. In view of Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Lim- ited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, AIR 2017 SC 5157, each appellants are entitled to receive Rs.15,000/- each for loss of state and funeral expenses.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8. Further, from impugned award, it is apparent that Tribunal has added 40%% as future prospects,
deducted  for personal & living expenses & has applied multiplier of 15.
These findings of the Tribunal have not been challenged by either of the parties.

9. Hence, in view of above, compensation awarded by Tribunal is recalculated as under:-

 3. Monthly loss of dependency (1/4th) 
 4. Annual loss of dependency   6. Multiplier of 15  7. Compensation for loss of spousal/parental/filial Rs.2,40,000/-
consortium 9. Compensation for loss of estate and towards Rs.30,000/-
funeral expenses 10.
Medical expenses Nil 11.

Total Compensation Rs.17,72,460/-
12.

Total compensation awarded by the Tribunal Rs.13,29,125/-
13.

Actual Enhancement Rs.4,43,335/-
10.

Hence, in view of above, including nature of injuries in the facts and circumstances of the case, it would be just and proper to enhance compensation by Rs.4,43,335/-
11.
Enhanced compensation Rs.4,43,335/- shall carry interest at the rate awarded by the Tribunal.
Other findings of the Tribunal shall remain intact.
12. Appellants have valued present appeal for Rs.1,00,00/-& have paid court fees accordingly.
Therefore, appellants shall be entitled to receive enhanced amount only after payment of deficit court fees.
13. Appeal filed by the appellants is partly allowed to the extent as indicated above and disposed of accordingly.
